visual_action: A montage of still and video shots of protesters, primarily young women, at a pro-choice rally in Washington, D.C., in front of the U.S. Supreme Court building. The protesters hold various handmade signs with slogans advocating for reproductive rights.

cast.name: Unnamed Protesters
cast.evidence: The video is a montage exclusively showing various protesters at a rally.

cast.name: U.S. Supreme Court
cast.evidence: The protest is visibly taking place in front of the U.S. Supreme Court building, which is the implicit target of the protest concerning abortion rights.

on_screen_text.text: MY BODY MY CHOICE HANDS OFF ♀
NOT YOUR UTERUS OR YOUR CHOICE
I AM NOT A BABY MAKING MACHINE
YOU CAN'T BAN ABORTION YOU CAN ONLY BAN SAFE ABORTION!

spoken_summary: There is no spoken dialogue in the video; the only audio is a music track.
audio_music: The video is set to a continuous, slowed-down electronic pop track, 'She Knows (slowed mix)' by Magy. The music has a determined but somewhat somber and serious tone, underscoring the gravity of the protest.
editing_pacing: The video is a quick-cut montage showing a series of different protesters and their signs, creating a sense of a large and unified movement.
cultural_references: The sign 'DON'T TREAD ON ME' featuring a drawing of a uterus is a reappropriation of the Gadsden flag, a historical American symbol often associated with libertarian and right-wing movements.
central_claim: The Democratic party stands with the numerous Americans who believe that abortion is healthcare, that bodily autonomy is a fundamental right, and that restricting abortion access is misogynistic.
intended_effect: To energize pro-choice supporters and demonstrate that the Democratic party is aligned with the widespread public movement for reproductive rights.
